instruction: Turn off tap-to-click for the touchpad in Ubuntu's settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling tap-to-click for touchpad. Config sets tap-to-click to true initially, user must change it to false. Evaluator checks gsettings value is 'false'. No custom functions needed - uses existing get_vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses get_vm_command_line getter to execute the gsettings command that reads the tap-to-click setting
The exact_match metric is appropriate for verifying boolean gsettings values
Expected value 'false\n' correctly includes the newline character that gsettings outputs
Complete coverage: the single-step instruction requirement (disable tap-to-click) is fully verified by checking the setting is false
Data flow is semantically correct: gsettings command output → exact string comparison → verification result
No state timing issues: gsettings values persist immediately and are reliably readable
